15	| `src/api/client.ts` | The only place that calls `fetch`: one typed function per endpoint, using `shared/` types. |
16	| `src/styles/` | `tokens.css` (copied design tokens) plus app styles built only from those tokens. |
17	| `shared/types.ts` | Domain entities and API request/response types shared by client and server. |
18	| `shared/<topic>.ts` | Pure business/validation logic (no I/O), with `<topic>.test.ts` beside it when the brief needs unit tests. No fixed entity names or pricing module is required. |
19	| `server/index.ts` | Boots Express: `GET /api/health`, `POST /api/reset`, `registerRoutes(app)`, unknown `/api/*` → 404 JSON, static `dist/` + SPA fallback. Rarely needs edits. |
20	| `server/routes/index.ts` | `registerRoutes(app)` mounts one router per resource. |
21	| `server/routes/<resource>.ts` | `express.Router()` for one resource. Thin handlers: parse the request, call the service, send status and body. |
22	| `server/services/<resource>.ts` | Store reads/writes and invariants for one resource, reusing `shared/` logic. |
23	| `server/db.ts` | JSON-file store: `readDb<T>()` returns the whole dataset (mutate it, then `writeDb(db)`), `resetDb()` restores the seed. |
24	| `server/data/seed.json` | Resolved domain seed copied from `../requirements/seed.json`. The original optional input stays unchanged. `server/data/db.json` is the live copy. |
25	| `e2e/` | Playwright specs. |
26	| `visual-evidence/` | Desktop/mobile PNGs for each target in `../design/visual-plan.json`, outside `test-results/`. |
27	
28	Create only the folders this product needs: a single-screen tool may have one page and no server resources.
29	Imports between files are extensionless (`import { x } from './db'`).
30	
31	## Code structure
32	
33	- One responsibility per file. Split a file before it passes about 200 lines; never collect every page, component or endpoint in one catch-all file.
34	- Name files and symbols after the product's domain (`BookingCard.tsx`, `routes/bookings.ts`, `shared/pricing.ts`), not `utils`, `helpers` or `misc`.
35	- Keep each rule in one place: calculations and validation in `shared/`, store access in `server/services/`. Components and route handlers call them instead of re-implementing them.
36	- Strict types end to end: no `any`, `@ts-ignore` or non-null assertions to silence errors.
37	- Small functions with intention-revealing names and early returns; named constants instead of repeated literals for statuses and limits.
38	- No dead or commented-out code, unused exports or debug logging.
39	
40	## Commands (run from this directory, one plain command at a time)
41	
42	| Command | What it does |
43	|---|---|
44	| `npm run build` | Type-check (`tsc`) then `vite build` into `dist/` |
45	| `npx vitest run` | Unit tests (`{src,server,shared}/**/*.test.ts(x)`); missing tests fail |
46	| `npx playwright test` | Builds, starts the server on port 3100, runs `e2e/`; add `--grep "<case-id>"` to run one case |
47	| `npm start` | Production server on `PORT` (default 3000) serving API + `dist/` — long-running, do not run it yourself |
48	
49	## Verification contract
50	
51	Keep one Chromium project and one worker: every test resets the same JSON store.
52	Call `POST /api/reset` in `beforeEach`; do not run mutation tests in parallel.
53	Acceptance tests belong in `e2e/case-<id>.spec.ts` with exact IDs from
54	`../requirements/acceptance.json`. Cases can be supplied by the brief or derived
55	from requested behavior when the brief has no explicit tests. Additional tests belong in
56	`journey.spec.ts`, `edge-cases.spec.ts`, `smoke.spec.ts`, and `visual.spec.ts`.
57	Do not change official expected values or hide failures with retries or skips.
58	
59	Read `../requirements/product.json` for the actual roles, entities and primary
60	journey; anonymous and single-screen products are supported. Never introduce
61	an unrelated marketplace, approval flow, money formula or persona switcher.
62	For static presentation with no meaningful pure logic, the reviewed product may
63	set `unit_tests_required: false` and explain `unit_test_reason`; the runner marks
64	unit verification not applicable only if no existing unit files need execution.
65	
66	The desktop viewport is 1440×900. Visual tests also use 390×844 via
67	`page.setViewportSize`, preserving one project and sequential resets. The
68	designer chooses 1–3 representative screens or states in `../design/visual-plan.json`.
69	Capture every target in both sizes as `visual-evidence/{desktop|mobile}-{target.id}.png`.
70	Use `page.screenshot({ path, fullPage: true, animations: 'disabled' })`, attach
71	the PNG with `testInfo.attach`, and wait for actual content and loaded images
72	before capture. Assert no horizontal page overflow. Do not use fixed sleeps.
73	
74	Screenshots support a separate visual review. After polish and final regression,
75	the visual reviewer reads every final planned PNG and records findings in
76	`../quality/visual-review.json`; the runner stamps the review and screenshot
77	and visual-plan hashes in `../quality/evidence.json` so stale evidence cannot pass.

# App skeleton

Stack: React 19 + react-router-dom 6 + Vite 8 (client), Express 4 run by tsx (server), TypeScript strict, Vitest, Playwright.
All dependencies are installed. Do not add packages.

## Layout

| Path | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `src/main.tsx` | Client entry. Already imports `styles/tokens.css` (design tokens). |
| `src/App.tsx` | App shell only: layout, navigation and the route table. No page bodies. |
| `src/pages/<Name>Page.tsx` | One file per route. Composes components and hooks; owns the page's loading/empty/error states. |
| `src/components/<Name>.tsx` | Reusable UI, one exported component per file. Data in through props, actions out through callbacks; no fetching. |
| `src/hooks/use<Name>.ts` | Data loading and stateful UI logic shared by pages. |
| `src/api/client.ts` | The only place that calls `fetch`: one typed function per endpoint, using `shared/` types. |
| `src/styles/` | `tokens.css` (copied design tokens) plus app styles built only from those tokens. |
| `shared/types.ts` | Domain entities and API request/response types shared by client and server. |
| `shared/<topic>.ts` | Pure business/validation logic (no I/O), with `<topic>.test.ts` beside it when the brief needs unit tests. No fixed entity names or pricing module is required. |
| `server/index.ts` | Boots Express: `GET /api/health`, `POST /api/reset`, `registerRoutes(app)`, unknown `/api/*` → 404 JSON, static `dist/` + SPA fallback. Rarely needs edits. |
| `server/routes/index.ts` | `registerRoutes(app)` mounts one router per resource. |
| `server/routes/<resource>.ts` | `express.Router()` for one resource. Thin handlers: parse the request, call the service, send status and body. |
| `server/services/<resource>.ts` | Store reads/writes and invariants for one resource, reusing `shared/` logic. |
| `server/db.ts` | JSON-file store: `readDb<T>()` returns the whole dataset (mutate it, then `writeDb(db)`), `resetDb()` restores the seed. |
| `server/data/seed.json` | Resolved domain seed copied from `../requirements/seed.json`. The original optional input stays unchanged. `server/data/db.json` is the live copy. |
| `e2e/` | Playwright specs. |
| `visual-evidence/` | Desktop/mobile PNGs for each target in `../design/visual-plan.json`, outside `test-results/`. |

Create only the folders this product needs: a single-screen tool may have one page and no server resources.
Imports between files are extensionless (`import { x } from './db'`).

## Code structure

- One responsibility per file. Split a file before it passes about 200 lines; never collect every page, component or endpoint in one catch-all file.
- Name files and symbols after the product's domain (`BookingCard.tsx`, `routes/bookings.ts`, `shared/pricing.ts`), not `utils`, `helpers` or `misc`.
- Keep each rule in one place: calculations and validation in `shared/`, store access in `server/services/`. Components and route handlers call them instead of re-implementing them.
- Strict types end to end: no `any`, `@ts-ignore` or non-null assertions to silence errors.
- Small functions with intention-revealing names and early returns; named constants instead of repeated literals for statuses and limits.
- No dead or commented-out code, unused exports or debug logging.

## Commands (run from this directory, one plain command at a time)

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `npm run build` | Type-check (`tsc`) then `vite build` into `dist/` |
| `npx vitest run` | Unit tests (`{src,server,shared}/**/*.test.ts(x)`); missing tests fail |
| `npx playwright test` | Builds, starts the server on port 3100, runs `e2e/`; add `--grep "<case-id>"` to run one case |
| `npm start` | Production server on `PORT` (default 3000) serving API + `dist/` — long-running, do not run it yourself |

## Verification contract

Keep one Chromium project and one worker: every test resets the same JSON store.
Call `POST /api/reset` in `beforeEach`; do not run mutation tests in parallel.
Acceptance tests belong in `e2e/case-<id>.spec.ts` with exact IDs from
`../requirements/acceptance.json`. Cases can be supplied by the brief or derived
from requested behavior when the brief has no explicit tests. Additional tests belong in
`journey.spec.ts`, `edge-cases.spec.ts`, `smoke.spec.ts`, and `visual.spec.ts`.
Do not change official expected values or hide failures with retries or skips.

Read `../requirements/product.json` for the actual roles, entities and primary
journey; anonymous and single-screen products are supported. Never introduce
an unrelated marketplace, approval flow, money formula or persona switcher.
For static presentation with no meaningful pure logic, the reviewed product may
set `unit_tests_required: false` and explain `unit_test_reason`; the runner marks
unit verification not applicable only if no existing unit files need execution.

The desktop viewport is 1440×900. Visual tests also use 390×844 via
`page.setViewportSize`, preserving one project and sequential resets. The
designer chooses 1–3 representative screens or states in `../design/visual-plan.json`.
Capture every target in both sizes as `visual-evidence/{desktop|mobile}-{target.id}.png`.
Use `page.screenshot({ path, fullPage: true, animations: 'disabled' })`, attach
the PNG with `testInfo.attach`, and wait for actual content and loaded images
before capture. Assert no horizontal page overflow. Do not use fixed sleeps.

Screenshots support a separate visual review. After polish and final regression,
the visual reviewer reads every final planned PNG and records findings in
`../quality/visual-review.json`; the runner stamps the review and screenshot
and visual-plan hashes in `../quality/evidence.json` so stale evidence cannot pass.

All five failures are fixed, and the full Playwright suite now passes (29 of 29). That includes the visual captures, which were regenerated. I did not open the regenerated screenshots, so I haven't checked how they look.

**Cause:** `SessionProviderBody` in `src/hooks/useSession.tsx` had an effect that wrote the current user ID to localStorage after mount. The app mounts only after the users fetch returns, which is after the test's `openAs` helper has stored the target user. If the effect ran after that, it overwrote the stored user with the default (Alex Rivera). The page then loaded as a customer instead of Emma, Michael or Jordan, so these checks failed:
- The staff and admin routes showed "You don't have access to this page".
- `/customer/tickets` showed Alex's data instead of Emma's.
- The duplicate-ticket edge test booked as Alex, so Emma's ticket list came back empty.

**Fix:** I removed that effect and the `useEffect` import it left unused. `selectUser` already saves the choice when someone switches accounts, so nothing else needed to persist it.

**Changed files:** only `src/hooks/useSession.tsx`. I made no test corrections.

**Checks run:** `npm run build` passed, `npx vitest run` passed (42 tests in 6 files), and `npx playwright test` passed in full.

**Limitations:** I didn't re-run the earlier failing tests repeatedly to confirm the race is gone for good. The race happened in a very short window, so a clean full run is good evidence but not proof.
